title: Reflecting on feedback you gave too late
grammar: should have / shouldn't have (feedback e arrependimento sobre o passado)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a falar de arrependimentos e feedback sobre o passado com 'should have' e 'shouldn't have'. Em Gestão de Pessoas na Delta Ducon, isso ajuda você a rever decisões, admitir erros com maturidade e orientar a equipe sobre o que poderia ter sido feito de outra forma.
intro: As a people manager, you often look back and think about what you could have done differently. Maybe you gave feedback too late, or maybe you missed a warning sign in the team.
Today we use 'should have' and 'shouldn't have' plus a past participle to talk about the past with hindsight. These structures make your reviews at Delta Ducon honest and reflective.
introAudio: Hi, I am Renata from People Management. After our last performance review, I realised I should have praised the team sooner, and I shouldn't have waited so long to give feedback. Today we will learn to talk about the past this way. It is a great tool for honest one-to-one meetings.
vocab: You should have given him a warning first.
She deserved more praise for her clean work.
We should have finished the appraisal on time.
You shouldn't have hidden the delay from your manager.
He shouldn't have missed the deadline for the report.
She should have given us more notice before she left.
practice: You should have given him a clear ______ before the formal review.
warning
I should have offered more ______ for her careful work on the baghouse.
praise
We shouldn't have delayed the annual ______ for the whole team.
appraisal
You shouldn't have hidden the ______ from your manager.
delay
He should have met the ______ for the emissions report.
deadline
She should have given us more ______ before she resigned.
notice
The manager should have written a ______ after the first mistake.
warning
You should have given honest ______ in the one-to-one meeting.
praise

audio.title: Looking back on a hard month
audio.text: Last month was difficult, and I have learned a lot from it. I should have given the team feedback earlier, instead of waiting for the appraisal. I shouldn't have ignored the small signs of low morale on the shop floor. We should have praised the technicians for the clean audit. I shouldn't have missed our one-to-one meetings during the busy shift. Next time I will act sooner, because good feedback should never come too late.

readAloud: I should have given feedback much sooner.
You shouldn't have hidden the delay from me.
We should have praised the team after the audit.
She shouldn't have missed the deadline.
They should have warned us about the change.
fill: You should ___ told me about the problem sooner. (have)
We shouldn't have ___ his feedback in the meeting. (ignore)
She should have ___ the deadline for the report. (meet)
I should ___ given her more praise. (have)
They should have ___ the appraisal last month. (do)
He should have ___ us more notice before leaving. (give)
We shouldn't have ___ the safety warning. (skip)
qa: What should you have done differently?
I should have given feedback earlier.
Should you have waited so long?
No, I shouldn't have waited so long.
What shouldn't the team have done?
They shouldn't have hidden the delay.
Should the manager have praised them?
Yes, she should have praised them after the audit.
What should he have done about the deadline?
He should have warned us before missing it.
sentences: I should have given feedback much sooner.
You shouldn't have hidden the delay from your manager.
We should have praised the team after the clean audit.
She shouldn't have missed such an important deadline.
They should have warned us about the schedule change.
He shouldn't have skipped the safety training.
We should have finished the appraisal on time.
You should have given her more notice before the transfer.
grammarPoint: Use 'should have' + particípio passado para dizer o que era certo fazer no passado (mas não foi feito) e 'shouldn't have' + particípio para o que foi feito mas era errado. I should have given feedback sooner. — Eu deveria ter dado feedback antes. You shouldn't have hidden the delay. — Você não deveria ter escondido o atraso.
deepDive: A estrutura é sempre should/shouldn't + have + particípio passado (given, told, done, met), igual para todos os sujeitos. Na fala, 'should have' soa como 'should've' — mas nunca escreva 'should of'. Dica: use essa forma para feedback reflexivo e para admitir erros com elegância, sem culpar ninguém de forma dura.
examples: I should have given feedback sooner.
Eu deveria ter dado feedback antes.
You shouldn't have hidden the delay.
Você não deveria ter escondido o atraso.
We should have praised the team.
Nós deveríamos ter elogiado a equipe.
She shouldn't have missed the deadline.
Ela não deveria ter perdido o prazo.
They should have warned the supplier.
Eles deveriam ter avisado o fornecedor.
He shouldn't have skipped the review.
Ele não deveria ter faltado à avaliação.
I should have listened to her concern.
Eu deveria ter ouvido a preocupação dela.
We shouldn't have ignored the low morale.
Nós não deveríamos ter ignorado o baixo ânimo.
mistakes: I should have gave feedback sooner.
I should have given feedback sooner.
Após 'have' use o particípio 'given', não o passado 'gave'.
You should of told me.
You should have told me.
É 'should have', nunca 'should of'.
She shouldn't have missing the deadline.
She shouldn't have missed the deadline.
Use o particípio 'missed', não o gerúndio 'missing'.
We should have to praise the team.
We should have praised the team.
Não há 'to' aqui; é have + particípio.
He should have warn the supplier.
He should have warned the supplier.
Use o particípio 'warned', não a forma base.
quick: They should have ___ us a warning. (give)

celebrate.en: Great work. Reflecting honestly on the past is how managers grow — and now you can do it in clear English.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo trabalho. Refletir com honestidade sobre o passado é como os gestores crescem — e agora você faz isso em inglês claro.

title: Reporting what the candidate asked
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a relatar perguntas que outras pessoas fizeram, usando 'He asked how...' e 'She asked whether...'. Em Gestão de Pessoas na Delta Ducon, isso é essencial para resumir entrevistas, reportar dúvidas de candidatos e passar informação da equipe para a liderança.
intro: After an interview or a team meeting, you often need to report what people asked. You do not repeat their exact words — you summarise them.
Today we use reported questions: 'He asked how the interview went' and 'She asked whether we had hired anyone'. Notice the word order changes and we use 'if' or 'whether' for yes/no questions.
introAudio: Hello, I am Marcos from People Management. After yesterday's interviews, my director asked how the candidates had done, and she asked whether we had checked their references. Today we will learn to report questions like these. It makes your updates clear and professional.
vocab: The applicant asked whether the role was remote.
She asked how the interview had gone.
He asked whether the reference was positive.
They asked who was on the shortlist.
The candidate asked when the offer would arrive.
He asked what the role involved.
practice: The director asked how the ______ had gone.
interview
She asked whether the ______ had accepted the job.
applicant
He asked if the ______ from her old manager was positive.
reference
They asked who was on the ______ for the engineer position.
shortlist
The candidate asked when the ______ would arrive.
offer
He asked what the new ______ involved day to day.
role
The manager asked how many people were on the ______.
shortlist
She asked whether the ______ still wanted the position.
applicant

audio.title: After the interviews
audio.text: After the interviews, my director had many questions for me. She asked how each candidate had answered the technical questions. She asked whether we had checked their references. She also asked when the best applicant could start on the shop floor. I told her that one applicant had asked what the role involved and whether the shifts were flexible. In the end, she asked if I would prepare the offer by Friday.

readAloud: She asked how the interview had gone.
He asked whether we had checked the references.
They asked who was on the shortlist.
The candidate asked when the offer would arrive.
My manager asked if I had prepared the report.
fill: She asked whether we ___ hired anyone. (have)
He asked if the candidate ___ ready. (be)
I asked how many people ___ applied. (have)
She asked whether the offer ___ been sent. (have)
They asked when the training ___ start. (will)
qa: What did the director ask about the candidates?
She asked how they had done in the interview.
What did the applicant ask?
He asked whether the role was remote.
What did your manager ask about the references?
She asked if we had checked them.
What did they ask about the offer?
They asked when the offer would arrive.
What did she ask about the shortlist?
She asked how many people were on it.
sentences: She asked how the interview had gone.
He asked whether we had checked the references.
They asked who was on the shortlist.
The applicant asked what the role involved.
My director asked when the offer would be ready.
He asked if the candidate was still interested.
She asked how many people had applied.
They asked where the second interview would take place.
grammarPoint: Em perguntas reportadas, usamos a ordem de uma afirmação (sem inversão e sem do/does/did) e recuamos o tempo verbal. Para perguntas de sim/não, use 'if' ou 'whether'. He asked how the interview went. — Ele perguntou como foi a entrevista. She asked whether we had hired anyone. — Ela perguntou se tínhamos contratado alguém.
deepDive: Compare: 'How did it go?' vira 'He asked how it had gone' (sujeito antes do verbo, sem 'did'). 'Are you ready?' vira 'She asked whether I was ready'. O presente costuma virar passado e o passado vira 'had + particípio'. Dica: 'whether' e 'if' têm o mesmo sentido aqui, mas 'whether' soa um pouco mais formal em relatórios escritos.
examples: He asked how the interview had gone.
Ele perguntou como tinha sido a entrevista.
She asked whether we had hired anyone.
Ela perguntou se tínhamos contratado alguém.
They asked who was on the shortlist.
Eles perguntaram quem estava na lista de finalistas.
He asked what the role involved.
Ele perguntou o que a função envolvia.
I asked when the offer would arrive.
Eu perguntei quando a proposta chegaria.
She asked if the candidate was available.
Ela perguntou se o candidato estava disponível.
The director asked how many people had applied.
A diretora perguntou quantas pessoas tinham se candidatado.
He asked whether the shifts were flexible.
Ele perguntou se os turnos eram flexíveis.
mistakes: He asked how did the interview go.
He asked how the interview went.
Em perguntas reportadas não se usa 'did' nem a inversão.
She asked that we had hired anyone.
She asked whether we had hired anyone.
Para pergunta de sim/não use 'if' ou 'whether', não 'that'.
They asked who was on the shortlist?
They asked who was on the shortlist.
É uma afirmação relatada; não leva ponto de interrogação.
He asked what does the role involve.
He asked what the role involved.
Sem 'does'; use a ordem de afirmação e recue o tempo.
She asked me where was the meeting.
She asked me where the meeting was.
Sujeito antes do verbo: 'where the meeting was'.
quick: She asked whether we ___ checked the references. (have)
I asked if the candidate ___ ready. (be)
He asked when the offer ___ arrive. (will)

celebrate.en: Excellent. Reporting questions clearly keeps everyone informed after interviews and meetings — a core people-management skill you now have in English.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Relatar perguntas com clareza mantém todos informados após entrevistas e reuniões — uma habilidade central da gestão de pessoas que agora você tem em inglês.

title: Wishing things were different in the team
grammar: wish + past simple / wish + past perfect (desejos e arrependimentos)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a expressar desejos sobre o presente com 'wish + passado simples' e arrependimentos sobre o passado com 'wish + past perfect'. Em Gestão de Pessoas na Delta Ducon, isso ajuda você a falar com honestidade sobre o que gostaria de mudar na equipe, no clima e nas decisões já tomadas.
intro: Every manager sometimes wishes things were different. Maybe you wish the budget were bigger, or you wish you had hired someone last year.
Today we learn two structures: 'wish + past simple' for the present ('I wish morale were higher') and 'wish + past perfect' for regrets about the past ('I wish we had acted sooner').
introAudio: Hi, I am Sofia from People Management. I wish our retention were better this year, and I wish we had offered training earlier. Today we will learn to talk about wishes and regrets. It is a gentle, honest way to reflect on your team.
vocab: I wish our retention were better this year.
I wish we had a bigger training budget.
I wish team morale were higher this quarter.
I wish we had more headcount for the night shift.
I wish turnover had been lower last year.
I wish the workload were lighter for the team.
practice: I wish our ______ were better so fewer engineers left.
retention
I wish we had a bigger ______ for leadership training.
budget
I wish team ______ were higher after the restructure.
morale
I wish we had more ______ to cover every shift.
headcount
I wish ______ had been lower during the busy year.
turnover
I wish the ______ were lighter for the montage team.
workload
The manager wishes the training ______ had been approved.
budget
We wish ______ had not risen after the new contract.
turnover

audio.title: If only things were different
audio.text: Sometimes I sit at my desk and think about what I wish were different. I wish our retention were stronger, because we lose good technicians every year. I wish we had a bigger budget for training and development. Looking back, I wish we had listened to the team's concerns sooner. I wish turnover had been lower last year, and I wish morale were higher today. These wishes remind me to make better decisions from now on.

readAloud: I wish our retention were better.
I wish we had a bigger training budget.
I wish we had hired her last year.
I wish morale were higher this quarter.
I wish turnover had been lower.
fill: I wish I ___ more time for one-to-ones. (have)
I wish we ___ offered him a promotion last year. (have)
I wish the training budget ___ bigger. (be)
I wish we had ___ more people last year. (hire)
I wish turnover ___ been lower in that period. (have)
I wish I ___ given her feedback sooner. (have)
I wish the workload ___ lighter this month. (be)
qa: What do you wish were different now?
I wish our retention were stronger.
Do you wish you had a bigger budget?
Yes, I wish we had more money for training.
What do you regret about last year?
I wish we had listened to the team sooner.
Do you wish morale were higher?
Yes, I wish morale were much higher this quarter.
What do you wish you had done?
I wish I had promoted her earlier.
sentences: I wish our retention were better this year.
I wish we had a bigger budget for training.
I wish morale were higher after the change.
I wish we had hired more people last year.
I wish turnover had been lower in that period.
I wish the workload were lighter for the team.
I wish I had given her feedback sooner.
I wish we had listened to their concerns.
grammarPoint: Use 'wish + passado simples' para desejos sobre o presente (situação que você queria diferente agora) e 'wish + past perfect (had + particípio)' para arrependimentos sobre o passado. I wish morale were higher. — Eu queria que o ânimo fosse maior. I wish we had hired her. — Eu queria ter contratado ela / que tivéssemos contratado ela.
deepDive: Com o verbo 'to be', prefira 'were' para todos os sujeitos após 'wish' (I wish I were, I wish she were, I wish it were). Para o passado, é sempre 'had + particípio' (had hired, had listened). Dica: 'wish + present' fala do agora que você quer mudar; 'wish + past perfect' fala de algo que já passou e não dá mais para mudar.
examples: I wish our retention were better.
Eu queria que a retenção fosse melhor.
I wish we had a bigger budget.
Eu queria que tivéssemos um orçamento maior.
I wish morale were higher.
Eu queria que o ânimo fosse maior.
I wish we had hired her last year.
Eu queria que tivéssemos contratado ela no ano passado.
I wish turnover had been lower.
Eu queria que a rotatividade tivesse sido menor.
I wish the workload were lighter.
Eu queria que a carga de trabalho fosse menor.
I wish I had given feedback sooner.
Eu queria ter dado feedback antes.
I wish we had listened to the team.
Eu queria que tivéssemos ouvido a equipe.
mistakes: I wish morale was higher.
I wish morale were higher.
Após 'wish', prefira 'were' para todos os sujeitos.
I wish we would have more budget.
I wish we had more budget.
Para o presente use o passado simples, não 'would have'.
I wish we have hired her last year.
I wish we had hired her last year.
Arrependimento do passado pede 'had + particípio'.
I wish I gave feedback sooner.
I wish I had given feedback sooner.
Para o passado use 'had given', não o passado simples.
I wish turnover had be lower.
I wish turnover had been lower.
Use o particípio 'been' após 'had'.
quick: I wish we ___ a bigger budget. (have)
I wish we had ___ her last year. (hire)

celebrate.en: Well done. Expressing wishes and regrets with care helps you reflect and improve — and now you can say it all in English.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Expressar desejos e arrependimentos com cuidado ajuda você a refletir e melhorar — e agora você sabe dizer tudo isso em inglês.

title: Agreeing and disagreeing in team meetings
grammar: so do I / neither do I (concordar e discordar)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a concordar de forma curta e natural com 'So do I' e 'Neither do I'. Em Gestão de Pessoas na Delta Ducon, isso deixa as reuniões de equipe mais fluidas, mostra alinhamento com colegas e ajuda você a construir consenso rapidamente.
intro: In team meetings, people often share opinions and you want to agree quickly. Instead of repeating the whole sentence, you can say 'So do I' or 'Neither do I'.
Today we learn these short answers. 'So do I' agrees with a positive idea, and 'Neither do I' agrees with a negative one. We match the auxiliary verb: So am I, Neither did I, So can I.
introAudio: Hello, I am Pedro from People Management. When a colleague says he wants a calmer shift, I say 'So do I'. When someone says she doesn't like long meetings, I say 'Neither do I'. Today we will practise these quick, friendly answers. They make team meetings feel natural.
vocab: I agree that safety comes first, and so does she.
I work overtime sometimes, and so do you.
I prefer remote one-to-ones, and so does he.
I enjoy the leadership workshop, and so do they.
I dislike a long commute, and so does she.
I trust my colleagues, and so do you.
practice: I always ______ that safety must come first.
agree
I sometimes work ______ before a big deadline.
overtime
I prefer ______ one-to-ones on busy factory days.
remote
I really enjoy the monthly leadership ______.
workshop
I dislike a long ______ to the Diadema site.
commute
I trust every ______ on the emissions team.
colleague
We ______ that team morale must improve this year.
agree
I do not want to do ______ every single week.
overtime

audio.title: A quick team meeting
audio.text: In our team meeting today, everyone agreed easily. One technician said he wanted more training, and I said 'So do I'. Another said she didn't like the long commute, and her colleague said 'Neither do I'. When the supervisor said he was proud of the clean audit, we all said 'So are we'. Someone said she couldn't join Friday's workshop, and I said 'Neither can I'. It was a short meeting, because we agreed on almost everything.

readAloud: I like the workshops. So do I.
I don't enjoy long meetings. Neither do I.
I am proud of the team. So am I.
I didn't finish the report. Neither did I.
I can lead the review. So can I.
fill: I like team lunches. So ___ I. (do)
I don't enjoy long meetings. Neither ___ I. (do)
I am tired after the shift. So ___ I. (be)
She can lead the review. So ___ I. (can)
I didn't finish the appraisals. Neither ___ I. (do)
I have sent the feedback. So ___ I. (have)
I won't be late tomorrow. Neither ___ I. (will)
They work very hard. So ___ we. (do)
qa: I enjoy the team workshops.
So do I.
I don't like a long commute.
Neither do I.
I am proud of our clean audit.
So am I.
I didn't agree with that decision.
Neither did I.
I can join the review on Friday.
So can I.

a.label: So do I / So am I
a.placeholder: So do I. / So am I.

sentences: I like the leadership workshops. So do I.
I don't enjoy long meetings. Neither do I.
I am proud of the team. So am I.
I didn't finish the appraisals. Neither did I.
I can lead the review. So can I.
I have sent the feedback. So have I.
I won't be late again. Neither will I.
She trusts her colleagues. So do we.
grammarPoint: Use 'So + auxiliar + sujeito' para concordar com algo positivo e 'Neither + auxiliar + sujeito' para concordar com algo negativo. O auxiliar precisa combinar com o verbo da outra frase. I like it. — So do I. (Eu também.) I don't like it. — Neither do I. (Nem eu.)
deepDive: Escolha o auxiliar pelo verbo: com present simple use do/does (So do I), com passado use did (Neither did I), com 'to be' use am/is/are (So am I), com modais repita o modal (So can I, Neither will I), com present perfect use have/has (So have I). Atenção à ordem invertida: verbo antes do sujeito. Dica: 'Neither' já é negativo, então o verbo fica positivo (Neither do I, nunca 'Neither don't I').
examples: I like the workshops. So do I.
Eu gosto dos workshops. Eu também.
I don't enjoy long meetings. Neither do I.
Eu não gosto de reuniões longas. Nem eu.
I am proud of the team. So am I.
Eu tenho orgulho da equipe. Eu também.
I didn't agree with that. Neither did I.
Eu não concordei com aquilo. Nem eu.
I can lead the review. So can I.
Eu consigo conduzir a avaliação. Eu também.
I have finished the report. So have I.
Eu terminei o relatório. Eu também.
I won't be late. Neither will I.
Eu não vou me atrasar. Nem eu.
She works overtime. So does he.
Ela faz hora extra. Ele também.
mistakes: I like it. So I do.
I like it. So do I.
A ordem é invertida: 'So do I', com o verbo antes do sujeito.
I don't like it. So do I.
I don't like it. Neither do I.
Para concordar com o negativo use 'Neither', não 'So'.
I don't agree. Neither don't I.
I don't agree. Neither do I.
'Neither' já é negativo; o verbo fica positivo.
I am tired. So do I.
I am tired. So am I.
Com o verbo 'to be' repita 'am/is/are', não 'do'.
I didn't finish. Neither do I.
I didn't finish. Neither did I.
No passado use 'did': 'Neither did I'.
quick: I like the workshops. So ___ I. (do)
I don't like the commute. Neither ___ I. (do)
I am proud of them. So ___ I. (be)
I can join the review. So ___ I. (can)

celebrate.en: Great job. Quick, natural agreement builds rapport and keeps meetings flowing — and now you can do it in English.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo trabalho. Concordar de forma rápida e natural cria conexão e mantém as reuniões fluindo — e agora você faz isso em inglês.

title: Comparing two candidates and two options
grammar: both / neither / either (of) — comparar duas opções
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a comparar duas opções com 'both', 'neither' e 'either (of)'. Em Gestão de Pessoas na Delta Ducon, isso é essencial para discutir dois candidatos, dois turnos ou duas propostas e explicar decisões de contratação com clareza.
intro: In people management, you often choose between two options: two candidates, two shifts, two suppliers. You need clear words to compare them.
Today we learn 'both' (the two together), 'neither' (not one and not the other) and 'either' (one or the other). We also practise 'both of', 'neither of' and 'either of' before 'the' or 'them'.
introAudio: Hi, I am Lucia from People Management. This week we interviewed two engineers. Both candidates were strong, but neither of them could start immediately. In the end, either option would have worked for the team. Today we will learn to compare two choices in English.
vocab: Both candidates have the right experience.
Neither option fits our tight budget.
Either shift works well for the new technician.
Both suppliers can meet the deadline.
Neither proposal was approved by the client.
Either role would suit her strengths.
practice: Neither ______ was approved by the client in the end.
proposal
Both technicians can cover the early ______ this week.
shift
Either ______ would suit her leadership strengths.
role
We met one very strong ______ for the engineer position.
candidate
Neither ______ fits our tight training budget.
option
We compared one ______ with another before we ordered.
supplier
The night ______ starts at ten o'clock.
shift
Either ______ can start work on Monday morning.
candidate

audio.title: A hard hiring decision
audio.text: Last week we had to choose between two candidates for the emissions team. Both candidates were qualified, and both had good references. Unfortunately, neither of them could start before next month. Either option would have suited the role, so it was a hard choice. In the end, both managers agreed on the same person. Neither manager had any doubt, which made the final decision much easier.

readAloud: Both candidates are strong for the role.
Neither option fits our budget.
Either shift works for the new technician.
Both of the suppliers can meet the deadline.
Neither of them is available on Friday.
fill: ___ candidates are qualified for the role. (the two)
___ option fits our budget, so we must rethink. (not one)
___ shift works for me; you can choose. (one or the other)
___ of the suppliers can meet the deadline. (the two)
___ of the two proposals was approved. (none)
You can take ___ role; both are open. (one or the other)
___ engineers passed the safety test. (the two)
___ of them is available on Friday. (not one)
qa: Which candidate should we hire?
Both candidates are strong, so it is a hard choice.
Do either of the shifts work for you?
Yes, either shift works for me.
Were the proposals approved?
No, neither proposal was approved.
Can both suppliers meet the deadline?
Yes, both of them can deliver on time.
Is either candidate available on Monday?
Neither of them is free until next week.
sentences: Both candidates are strong for the role.
Neither option fits our tight budget.
Either shift works for the new technician.
Both of the suppliers can meet the deadline.
Neither of the two proposals was approved.
Either role would suit her strengths.
Both managers agreed on the same person.
Neither of them is available on Friday.
grammarPoint: Use 'both' para os dois juntos (com verbo no plural), 'neither' para nenhum dos dois (com verbo no singular) e 'either' para um ou outro (com verbo no singular). Antes de 'the' ou 'them' use 'of': both of the candidates, neither of them. Both candidates are strong. — Os dois candidatos são fortes. Neither option fits. — Nenhuma das duas opções serve.
deepDive: 'Both' pede verbo no plural (Both are ready); 'neither' e 'either' pedem verbo no singular (Neither is ready, Either works). Use 'of' quando vier 'the', 'these' ou um pronome: 'both of the shifts', 'neither of them'. Sem 'of', o substantivo vem direto: 'both shifts', 'neither shift'. Dica: 'neither' já carrega a negação, então não use outra palavra negativa na frase.
examples: Both candidates have good references.
Os dois candidatos têm boas referências.
Neither option fits our budget.
Nenhuma das duas opções cabe no orçamento.
Either shift works for the team.
Qualquer um dos dois turnos serve para a equipe.
Both of the suppliers delivered on time.
Os dois fornecedores entregaram no prazo.
Neither of them is available on Friday.
Nenhum dos dois está disponível na sexta.
Either role would suit her.
Qualquer um dos dois cargos serviria para ela.
Both managers agreed on the decision.
Os dois gestores concordaram com a decisão.
Neither proposal was approved.
Nenhuma das duas propostas foi aprovada.
mistakes: Both candidate is strong.
Both candidates are strong.
Com 'both' use o plural: 'candidates are'.
Neither options fit the budget.
Neither option fits the budget.
Com 'neither' use o singular: 'option fits'.
Either of them are available.
Either of them is available.
'Either of' pede verbo no singular: 'is'.
Both of candidates are good.
Both of the candidates are good.
Após 'both of' é preciso 'the' antes do substantivo.
Neither proposal wasn't approved.
Neither proposal was approved.
'Neither' já é negativo; não use outra negativa.
quick: ___ shift works for me. (one or the other)
___ of the suppliers can deliver. (the two)
___ of them is free on Friday. (not one)

celebrate.en: Well done. Comparing two options clearly is how managers explain fair decisions — and now you can do it with confidence in English.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Comparar duas opções com clareza é como os gestores explicam decisões justas — e agora você faz isso com confiança em inglês.
